title: Quant watchdog: staged recalibration + traffic-steering fallback for FP8/INT8 canaries
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build an automated watchdog and staged recovery path for FP8/INT8 canary rollouts. When a quantized canary degrades quality beyond configured tolerances (offline and online checks), the system should first attempt a targeted recalibration using live trace microbatches and then, if thresholds are still violated, perform progressive traffic-steering and automated fallback to a higher-precision variant or the FP16 baseline. The goal is to keep customer-facing latency and availability stable while minimizing rollback blast radius and enabling fast triage.
implementation_plan: Define canary metrics and thresholds: offline calibration delta (validationset PPL/QA), online shadow skew (response similarity score), safety filter fail rate, latency P99 increase, and error rate.

Add a lightweight 'recalibrate-on-failure' job: collect small reservoir of recent requests (configurable window), run fast post-quant calibration passes (per-layer scale re-estimation), and produce candidate reprofiled parameters without full model rebuild.

Implement watchdog orchestration component in serving plane that: subscribes to canary metric streams, triggers recalibration job on threshold breach, evaluates recalibrated candidate on a mirrored micro-traffic slice (shadow), and decides next action based on evaluation.

Traffic-steering policy: shift incremental percent of traffic away from canary to fallback variant (step-down schedule: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%), with automated hold and retry windows between steps.
Fallback targets: quantized variant with alternative quant profile (less aggressive clamp/scale) OR FP16/FP32 baseline depending on config and cost tier.

Observability & Telemetry: add per-canary diff dashboards (baseline vs canary for accuracy metrics, token-level deltas), export recalibration artefacts and scores to S3/Datadog, and surface actionable alert text in PagerDuty/Slack runbooks.
Safety & governance: require security review flag for private deployments; ensure no customer PII leaves VPC during recalibration (sampling rules and encryption-in-transit).
End-to-end tests: unit tests for decision logic, integration test with canary runner, and synthetic-data run that simulates drift/failure modes.
Rollout plan: start gated beta (internal + small set of customers), iterate on thresholds and calibration heuristics, then enable for all quantized rollouts.
Documentation: update runbooks, Console UX for canary controls, and SDK hooks for operators to annotate fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Watchdog triggers recalibration job automatically when online skew > configured threshold and records candidate artifacts.
Recalibrated candidate tested in shadow traffic with measurable accuracy improvement vs failing canary in >=75% of simulated failures.
If shadow candidate fails or absent, system progressively steers traffic to fallback variant following the step schedule without human intervention.
Rollback/fallback completes within configured SLO (max 3 minutes) and preserves availability for upstream customers.
Console shows clear canary status, reason for fallback, and links to recalibration artifacts and diffs.
End-to-end integration tests and synthetic scenarios pass in CI; performance regression < 5% CPU/GPU overhead when watchdog is idle.
risks: Recalibration with live traffic could introduce bias if sampling not representative; must isolate and limit sample sizes.
Automated traffic steering might exacerbate outages if fallback targets are under-provisioned; autoscaling policies must be validated.
Telemetry volume and storage cost from per-token diffs could grow large; need retention and aggregation strategy.
False positives from noisy online metrics could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; thresholds require tuning and hysteresis.
